title: Why ice cream gives you brain freeze
pause_note: Channel v5, Your Body, Explained. WEIRD hook: cone goes into the mouth at 0 s and the forehead flashes with pain by ~1.5 s; wrong guess (the brain is freezing) killed at ~4.5 s; reveal at ~7 s (palate vessels clamp then flood open); nerve shares the forehead (referred pain); the tongue fix (hedged: doctors suggest); loop to the cone; one-word question.

beats: The ice cream is in your mouth. So why does your forehead hurt?
Your brain is not freezing. Look at the roof of your mouth.
The cold makes its blood vessels clamp shut, then flood wide open.
The nerve that reports it also covers your forehead, so your brain blames the wrong spot.
In one trial, gulping it more than doubled the chance of getting one.
Doctors suggest pressing your tongue to the roof of your mouth, to warm it back up.
